About Zorawar

A name that
means strength.

Zorawar arrived on a January afternoon and changed everything. His name — rooted in the Punjabi tradition — means mighty, powerful, brave. He has earned every letter of it.

The first weeks were not easy. Zora was diagnosed with neonatal hepatitis, which dragged his jaundice far longer than expected. Because he wasn't feeding well, the jaundice wasn't clearing — the doctors called it breastfeeding jaundice. It was a difficult, exhausting loop to break. But we broke it, together.

He came in at 3.26 kg and has been climbing steadily since. We log every feed, celebrate every gram, and find meaning in every small moment — because after what we've been through, nothing feels small anymore.

A note for Zorawar

"You are the reason our hearts learned to hold more than we ever thought possible."

Your first weeks were harder than we had planned. Neonatal hepatitis, prolonged jaundice, slow weight gain — we faced all of it together. You fought through every feed, every blood test, every anxious night, without knowing any of it was a fight. We watched you get stronger, gram by gram and day by day, and we kept this record so that one day you'll know: every single moment was worth it, and we were watching, and we were so, so proud.

— Mama & Papa, always
